decisions.reason: As a prominently launched next-generation industrial printer in the firm’s core machinery business, it is a strategic platform product whose upside still justifies continued market presence despite nontrivial support costs.
This numbering module is a low-cost software complement to the installed printing base, so real-options logic favors keeping it available while demand across applications continues to be learned.
An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits the firm’s established coding portfolio, and although it may serve a narrower niche, the evidence does not yet warrant abandoning the option.
Because the app is a successor to an earlier solution and supports the wider coding ecosystem, the firm would likely keep it on the market unless usage clearly disappoints.
Inline code verification is closely adjacent to the firm’s marking and coding systems, so management would usually retain it as a complementary option while customer adoption becomes clearer.
Print layout software is a relatively inexpensive complement to hardware sales and was launched prominently, making it sensible for a large firm to keep it rather than exit early.
